items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: And they came down and they checked all the bands and they selected our band, the best one. So they started us to coming up into Cincinnati.

ctx.x: And we had a crippled fellow on the clarinet. I can't think of his name now. He's dead. And sometimes we have George Lewis and drag. Well, the piano player, I didn't know his name. Then we had another fellow by the name of Alfred used to play sax with us sometime when we couldn't get clarinet. Well, how I come to get into the George Lewis band, I played with Eddie Morris back at Linfans, back on Canal Boulevard. One Sunday afternoon. And George had a job at the corner from Drag's house. And he needed a drummer.…
Well, somebody told me a few months ago, Reverend Kershaw was a professor. Did you ever hear any of them?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: Then Reverend Kershaw in the meantime when we was playing out there they came down here and heard different bands and they selected our band.

ctx.x: No trombone? Yeah, Jim Robinson. Oh Jim, yeah. Well we stayed there for about two years I'd say. Yeah. Then Reverend Kershaw in the meantime when we was playing out there they came down here and heard different bands and they selected our band.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Well, they started from Myrtleville in Boivin, where we was playing there, Almerocka, and went down in every place that had a band. And they selected us.

ctx.x: Yes. Would that be the Parisian Room?

The Parisian Room, yeah. Yeah, the Parisian Room. Well, we played there one Saturday night, and the Almerocka Club had warned us. So, after we got through playing there was this fellow, Eddie Kidd Wolf, former friend, a dry spider, and his partner was named Frank. He was an Italian. Well, when we got through playing at the Parisian Room, we went there and finished out the night, because we knocked off at 12 o'clock at the Parisian Room. And we went there and played a couple hours until 2 o'clock in the morning.…
